items.title: George "Tex" Stephens Interview, 1995-08-29
items.q: And then Amos Milburn left the Dewdrop and came down to Foster's Club and Hotel, and they battled there for a while.

ctx.x: What about some of the, I was talking about the ancillary clubs, and like, you know, like Foster's? How was Foster's?

George Foster was two blocks from the Doudrop, still right there on LaSalle Street. George Foster had the little downtown club, I mean the uptown club, and he wasn't the promoter that Frank Pena was. He was the guy who fell in line. But he started bringing in, like, well he had brought in Roy Brown, then he had a combination with Roy Brown, and went on the Irish with the first Battle of the Blues that I could recall in the city of New Orleans. That went on for around about maybe five hours between the two of…
Straight A, not straight A's. Something about Aces.

Oh, I'm fine. It'll pick up. It always picks up. Okay, we'll continue with Tech Stevens. This is the, let's make sure this one's working. Okay, continuing with Tech Stevens. Today is August the 23rd. I think it's 23rd, Saturday 23rd. We're at Tulane University. My name's Tad Jones, and we're with Techs. So we were going to pick up, go back and listen to, you know, talk about some other, some things that we left off.

We left off. Yeah, well let's fill in where we left off. Let's go back to the 40s and we'll update things. Some of the things we didn't cover, like when Oyskin Hawkins came here in 1949. He played at the Booker T. Washington Auditorium. And incidentally, Mabel Scott played at Foster's Rainbow Room, and Gate Mouth Brown played together. And then they went over to the Dewdrop, and they did a midnight show like that was back there in 1949. And I think I discussed with you earlier about Amos Milburn and Winoni Harris…
